description: Full rewrite of the two Spanish tutorials to be CDK-centric, plus a minimal README touch-up. EXACTLY TWO tutorial markdown files at repo root (no third doc); Mermaid diagrams embedded. 01-metricas-y-logs.md pivots from manual AWS-CLI EC2 provisioning to a CDK flow (configure `stay` profile -> cdk bootstrap -> obtain IP + -c allowedCidr -> cdk synth/deploy -> wait -> verify user-data/containers Up -> access Grafana -> build CPU dashboard -> build API-responses dashboard -> traffic -> verify -> troubleshooting -> security -> cost -> cdk destroy). 02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md builds on the deployed infra (no re-deploy), adds a brief 'why OpenTelemetry+Jaeger and NOT X-Ray' paragraph, keeps 100% OTel->Collector->Jaeger wiring, and documents Jaeger access via SSM port-forward / SSH tunnel to 16686 and trace exploration. DEPENDS ON FEAT-004 (references the cdk/ paths, context args, CfnOutputs, and user-data behavior). Reuse the existing dashboard-building and trace-exploration prose; only the deploy/bootstrap sections change shape. Keep the pedagogical format (que/por que/comando exacto/directorio/resultado esperado/como comprobar/que revisar). Do NOT fabricate command outputs; label 'resultado esperado' distinctly. Do NOT mention or implement X-Ray except the one-paragraph 'why not X-Ray' rationale.
steps: Rewrite 01-metricas-y-logs.md with sections IN ORDER: (1) objetivos de aprendizaje; (2) arquitectura + Mermaid del flujo CDK(Python) -> CloudFormation -> EC2(user-data) -> Docker Compose arrancando TODOS los servicios (api, service-b, Prometheus, Loki, Alloy, Grafana, node_exporter, OTel Collector, Jaeger) en la red obsnet; (3) enfoque: todo con CDK, NO montaje local (un parrafo); (4) requisitos previos (AWS CLI v2, Node.js para el cdk CLI aunque la app sea Python, Python 3.12, `npm i -g aws-cdk` v2); (5) configurar el perfil `stay` (account 550428926318, user arn:aws:iam::550428926318:user/JuanHoyos, region us-east-1); (6) `cdk bootstrap aws://550428926318/us-east-1 --profile stay` (que hace, bucket/rol que crea, por que es prerequisito); (7) obtener la IP del estudiante con `curl -s https://checkip.amazonaws.com` y pasarla como `-c allowedCidr=<ip>/32`; (8) `cd cdk && pip install -r requirements.txt`, `cdk synth` (validacion local sin crear nada) y luego `cdk deploy -c allowedCidr=... --profile stay` (lo ejecuta EL ESTUDIANTE; el tutorial NO lo ejecuta) — enumerar los recursos que crea (VPC lookup, SG obs-lab-sg, IAM role obs-lab-ec2-role + instance profile, EC2 t3.small, EBS gp3 20GB, asset en S3) y los CfnOutputs (PublicIp, GrafanaUrl, JaegerTunnelCommand, SsmSessionCommand).

Continue 01-metricas-y-logs.md: (9) verificar que el user-data termino y los contenedores estan Up — SSM Session Manager (`aws ssm start-session --target <id> --profile stay`) o SSH, `docker ps` (9 servicios), y revisar `/var/log/cloud-init-output.log`; (10) acceder a Grafana por IP publica `http://<ip>:3000` (admin / password del .env, nota: el .env lo genera user-data); (11) construir paso a paso el DASHBOARD DE CPU desde node_exporter (aclarar node_exporter = metricas del SO, NO CloudWatch) con PromQL `100 - (avg by(instance)(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[5m])) * 100)`, unidades %, leyenda, refresh; (12) construir paso a paso el DASHBOARD DE RESPUESTAS DE LA API: latencia p50/p90/p99 con `histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by(le,route)(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))`, solicitudes totales y por endpoint `sum by(route)(rate(api_requests_total[5m]))`, codigos HTTP 2xx/4xx/5xx via `api_requests_by_status_class_total`, tasa de error y req/s (reutilizar el PromQL de config/grafana/dashboards/api.json); (13) generar trafico con `python scripts/load_test.py --base-url http://<ip>:8000`; (14) verificacion de metricas y logs (Loki en Grafana `{service="obs-lab-api"} | json`).

Finish 01-metricas-y-logs.md: (15) troubleshooting (user-data no termino -> revisar cloud-init-output.log; puertos; SG mal acotado; from_lookup pide credenciales); (16) seguridad (SG acotado a la IP del estudiante; SSM vs SSH; que puertos se abren y por que; 9090/3100/4317/4318/16686 internos por tunel); (17) estimacion de costes (EC2 t3.small, EBS gp3 20GB, IP publica, transferencia; `cdk destroy` elimina TODO; `stop` NO borra EBS/IP; sin NAT/ALB); (18) limpieza con `cdk destroy -c allowedCidr=... --profile stay` y nota de NO tocar los Lambdas soc-challenge-*/SocChallenge-*/lumen-production-*. Mantener el formato pedagogico por paso y NO fabricar salidas.

Rewrite 02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md with sections IN ORDER: (1) objetivos; (2) arquitectura de trazas + Mermaid (api -> service-b, OTel SDK -> OTel Collector -> Jaeger, todo dentro de la EC2); (3) diferencias metrica vs log vs traza (reutilizar tabla); (4) por que OpenTelemetry+Jaeger y por que NO X-Ray en este lab — UN parrafo breve (self-hosted, coste ~0, control total, estandar abierto); NO implementar X-Ray; (5) recorrido de la peticion (Alternativa B, segundo contenedor service-b) + tabla comparativa breve vs Lambda; (6) como se instrumento con OpenTelemetry (FastAPI + httpx auto-instrumentation, propagacion W3C traceparent, un span manual service-b.work; no duplicar spans; mantener nota setuptools==75.*); (7) config del OTel Collector (otlp receivers, memory_limiter/resource/batch, exporter otlp a jaeger:4317, COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true; exportador nativo jaeger eliminado en contrib 0.109).

Finish 02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md: (8) acceso a Jaeger via SSM port-forward (`aws ssm start-session --target <id> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters '{"portNumber":["16686"],"localPortNumber":["16686"]}' --profile stay`) o tunel SSH `-L 16686:localhost:16686` (comando exacto); (9) ejecutar `/checkout` y `/checkout?slow=1` contra la IP publica; (10) explorar la traza en Jaeger (lista, abrir una, spans padre-hijo, confirmar que api y service-b comparten el MISMO trace_id, tiempo por servicio, cuello de botella de latencia); (11) correlacion metricas->logs->trazas (trace_id en los logs JSON, Loki derivedFields -> Jaeger); (12) verificacion de la solucion; (13) troubleshooting (user-data no termino, Collector no exporta, puertos); (14) seguridad y costes adicionales (service-b ~$0 extra; Jaeger en la misma EC2); (15) limpieza de recursos adicionales (ya cubierta por `cdk destroy` del stack unico). NO fabricar salidas; 'resultado esperado' distinguido.

Update README.md to point to the two tutorials and the cdk/ directory, presenting CDK as the PRIMARY path and relabeling the docker-compose quick start as the OPTIONAL offline path. Confirm there are EXACTLY TWO tutorial markdown files at repo root (01-metricas-y-logs.md, 02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md) plus README.md; no third tutorial/architecture markdown.
acceptance_criteria: 01-metricas-y-logs.md is CDK-centric: it documents configuring the `stay` profile, `cdk bootstrap`, obtaining the IP and passing `-c allowedCidr`, `cdk synth`/`cdk deploy`, verifying user-data finished and containers are Up (SSM/SSH + docker ps + cloud-init-output.log), accessing Grafana by public IP, building the CPU dashboard (node_exporter, clarified vs CloudWatch) and the API-responses dashboard (latency p50/p90/p99, request count, HTTP status codes, error rate, req/s), cost, security, and cleanup via `cdk destroy`. It no longer presents local Docker as the main path and contains no `aws ec2 run-instances` manual-provisioning flow as the primary path.

02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md builds on the deployed infra (no re-deploy), contains the one-paragraph 'why OpenTelemetry+Jaeger and NOT X-Ray' rationale, keeps the OTel->Collector->Jaeger (jaeger:4317, COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true) wiring, documents Jaeger access via SSM port-forward / SSH tunnel to 16686, and walks through exploring a trace with a shared trace_id and parent-child spans.

Neither tutorial adds, implements, or recommends AWS X-Ray (the only X-Ray mention is the brief rationale for NOT using it). No fabricated command outputs; 'resultado esperado' is distinguished from verified results.

Exactly two tutorial markdown files exist at repo root plus README.md (no third doc); README points to both tutorials and cdk/ with CDK as the primary path; AWS facts (profile stay, account 550428926318, user JuanHoyos, us-east-1, key pair ec2-docker-api-key, prefix obs-lab, tag Project=obs-lab) appear verbatim; the student IP is always obtained with `curl -s https://checkip.amazonaws.com` (no bare placeholder).
verification: grep -n '^## ' 01-metricas-y-logs.md (confirm ordered CDK sections: bootstrap, allowedCidr, cdk deploy, verify containers, CPU dashboard, API dashboard, cdk destroy)
grep -q 'cdk deploy' 01-metricas-y-logs.md && grep -q 'cdk bootstrap' 01-metricas-y-logs.md && grep -q 'checkip.amazonaws.com' 01-metricas-y-logs.md && grep -q 'cdk destroy' 01-metricas-y-logs.md
findings:
DONE. Fully rewrote the TWO Spanish tutorials at repo root to be CDK-centric and updated README.md to present CDK as the primary path (docker-compose relabeled as an optional offline appendix). Exactly two tutorial markdowns + README exist; no third doc. Used the FEAT-004 facts verbatim (profile stay, account 550428926318, user JuanHoyos, us-east-1, key pair ec2-docker-api-key, prefix obs-lab, tag Project=obs-lab) and the real CfnOutput names (PublicIp, PublicDnsName, GrafanaUrl, SsmSessionCommand, JaegerTunnelCommand). Student IP always via `curl -s https://checkip.amazonaws.com`; `-c allowedCidr=$(...)/32` on synth/deploy/destroy. No fabricated outputs ('resultado esperado' labeled distinctly). No X-Ray except the one-paragraph 'why NOT X-Ray' rationale in 02 section 4.

01-metricas-y-logs.md FINAL SECTION LIST (## headers): Indice; 1 Objetivos de aprendizaje; 2 Arquitectura: de CDK a los contenedores (Mermaid CDK->CloudFormation->EC2 user-data->Docker Compose, 9 servicios en obsnet); 3 Enfoque: todo con CDK, nada en local; 4 Requisitos previos (AWS CLI v2, Node.js para el cdk CLI, Python 3.12, npm i -g aws-cdk); 5 Configuracion de AWS CLI y perfil stay; 6 Bootstrap del entorno CDK (cdk bootstrap aws://550428926318/us-east-1 --profile stay); 7 Obtener tu IP y pasar -c allowedCidr (curl -s https://checkip.amazonaws.com); 8 Desplegar la infraestructura (cdk synth y cdk deploy) con tabla de recursos y CfnOutputs; 9 Verificar que el user-data termino y los contenedores estan Up (SSM/SSH + docker ps 9 servicios + /var/log/cloud-init-output.log); 10 Acceder a Grafana por la IP publica (http://<ip>:3000, .env generado por user-data); 11 Construir el dashboard de CPU (node_exporter, clarified vs CloudWatch, PromQL 100 - (avg by(instance)(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode=idle}[5m]))*100)); 12 Construir el dashboard de respuestas de la API (req/s, por endpoint, p50/p90/p99 histogram_quantile, 2xx/4xx/5xx, por codigo HTTP, tasa de error); 13 Generacion de trafico (python scripts/load_test.py --base-url http://<ip>:8000); 14 Verificacion de metricas y logs (Loki {service=obs-lab-api} | json); 15 Troubleshooting; 16 Seguridad: puertos, SSM y tuneles; 17 Estimacion de costes; 18 Limpieza con cdk destroy.

02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md FINAL SECTION LIST (## headers): Indice; 1 Objetivos de aprendizaje; 2 Arquitectura de trazas (Mermaid api->service-b, OTel SDK->Collector->Jaeger dentro de la EC2 desplegada en Parte 1); 3 Diferencias entre metrica, log y traza; 4 Por que OpenTelemetry + Jaeger y no X-Ray (un parrafo: self-hosted, coste ~0, estandar abierto, control total; NO implementar X-Ray); 5 Diseno del recorrido y el servicio service-b (Alternativa B vs Lambda, tabla); 6 Instrumentacion con OpenTelemetry (y propagacion W3C traceparent; setuptools==75.* nota; OTEL_ENABLED=true lo pone el user-data); 7 Configuracion del OTel Collector (otlp receivers, memory_limiter/resource/batch, exporter otlp a jaeger:4317, COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true, exportador jaeger eliminado en contrib 0.109); 8 Acceder a Jaeger (SSM AWS-StartPortForwardingSession a 16686 / SSH -L 16686:localhost:16686); 9 Ejecutar peticiones /checkout (y ?slow=1); 10 Explorar la traza en Jaeger (spans padre-hijo, mismo trace_id, cuello de botella service-b.work); 11 Correlacion metricas->logs->trazas; 12 Verificacion; 13 Troubleshooting; 14 Seguridad y costes adicionales; 15 Limpieza de recursos adicionales (cubierta por cdk destroy del stack unico).

README.md: CDK presentada como ruta principal con flujo bootstrap/deploy/destroy, enlaces a ambos tutoriales y a cdk/; docker-compose relabel como 'Apendice opcional: arranque local (offline)'.

VERIFICATION RESULTS (all PASS): grep '^## ' confirms the ordered CDK sections in 01 (bootstrap, allowedCidr, cdk deploy, verify containers, CPU dashboard, API dashboard, cdk destroy). 01 contains cdk deploy / cdk bootstrap / checkip.amazonaws.com / cdk destroy. 01 X-Ray match count = 0 (removed the only incidental '(sin X-Ray)' note from a table so the hard rule holds). 02 contains AWS-StartPortForwardingSession + COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED + jaeger:4317; 02 X-Ray matches = 6, all inside the single 'why NOT X-Ray' rationale (section 4), as allowed. `ls *.md` = exactly 01-metricas-y-logs.md, 02-trazas-distribuidas-opentelemetry-jaeger.md, README.md.
